meta.title: How it works
meta.description: What a launch does on-chain, what it costs (gas), and what can never happen to your liquidity.

rules.title: How it works
rules.description: One transaction on Base, Robinhood Chain or Arc. Your token, a market, and a permanently locked liquidity position. You only pay gas.

launch.noSetup: No separate setup. No platform fee.

token.title: Your token is deployed
token.description: A plain ERC-20 with EIP-2612 permit. Fixed supply, 1 billion by default. No mint, no pause, no blacklist, no transfer tax, no owner.
token.label: default supply

market.title: A market opens
market.description: A Uniswap v4 pool pairs your token with ETH, TWIG on Base, GITLAWB or USDG on Robinhood Chain, a tokenized stock (Coinbase stocks on Base, Robinhood Stock Tokens on Robinhood Chain), or USDC on Arc. No hook. The pool starts at the market cap you pick.
market.label: Uniswap pool

lock.title: The liquidity position is locked
lock.description: 100% of the supply goes into one single-sided position at launch. Its NFT is minted to an ownerless locker that has no function to withdraw, transfer or shrink it. Ever.
lock.label: deposited at launch

fees.title: Fee routing is written in
fees.description: The trading fee you choose (0%, 1% or 3%) goes 100% to the beneficiaries you name, or is burned if you name none. Fixed at launch, unchangeable.
fees.label: your trading fee

launch.note: The position stays locked. Tokens remain tradeable.

fees.heading: Know where it goes.
fees.gasToNetwork: Gas is paid to the network.
fees.creatorChooses: The creator chooses the trading fee
fees.zero: No pool trading fee. Network gas still applies. Nobody earns fees from volume, including the creator.
fees.oneOrThreeBody: Uniswap charges it on every trade and it accrues to the locked position. The platform takes no share.
fees.fixed: Beneficiaries and shares are set at launch and can never be changed. A promise like “half the fees go to this address” is enforced by the contract, not by us.
fees.collectHeading: Anyone can collect. The routing decides who receives.
fees.collect: Press Collect on the token page. Accrued fees leave the pool and are paid straight to the beneficiaries in the same transaction, or burned to {dead} if the launch has no beneficiary.
fees.credited: If a beneficiary cannot receive the payment, their share is credited to them and can be claimed any time. It is never lost and never blocks the others.

noFee.title: No platform fee
noFee.description: There is no fee address, fee variable or treasury anywhere in the factory or the locker. Nothing to switch on later. It cannot be added to immutable code.

noWithdrawal.title: No liquidity withdrawal
noWithdrawal.description: Nobody can remove liquidity: not the creator, not us. Collecting fees removes zero liquidity.

noPremine.title: No pre-mine
noPremine.description: Every token starts inside the pool. There is no creator-reserved allocation.

noAdmin.title: No admin
noAdmin.description: No owner, no pause, no upgrade, no allowlist. The contracts are the same for everyone, forever.

anyPair.title: Any token as the pair
anyPair.description: The contracts accept any ERC-20 as the pair. The site lists community pairs after public checks (/pairs); a pair it does not list still trades, shown as an unlisted pair with no USD price.

points.intro: Points measure reputation on openlaunch. They have no cash value, are not a token and not a promise of one, cannot be transferred or sold, and the rules can change between seasons. Wallets that game the system lose their points. Everything is computed from the chain every hour; the rules below are the whole of it.

realBuyer.question: What counts as a real buyer?
realBuyer.who: A wallet whose first buy of a token was ${minTradeUsd} or more, made after the launch block, the next {sniperBlocks} blocks and the first {sniperSeconds} seconds. The wallet must receive the tokens of that buy itself (a relayer or router that only passed them on is not a buyer). Never the launcher, a fee recipient, a wallet that got the token by transfer from either, or a wallet kept off points. A real holder is a real buyer with ${holderMinUsd} or more (${verifiedHolderMinUsd} for a qualifying profile, below) of that first buy still in the wallet.
realBuyer.holding: Holding is judged per buy: whenever tokens leave a wallet (sold, or moved to any other wallet), the most recently received ones go first. So selling a later buy does not touch an earlier one, tokens sent in from another wallet never stand in for a buy, and moving a position out counts the same as selling it. Only tokens priced in a quote we can price count.

creators.question: How do creators earn?
creators.holders: On any token you launched, only what happens during the season counts. Each real holder who first bought this season and still holds a day later earns you {verifiedHolder} points if their profile qualifies (below), or {holder} if not; a week later, half again. Each holder counts once for you, on whichever of your tokens they are worth most.
creators.fees: Fees on buys by traders with a qualifying profile earn {creatorFeePointsPerUsd} points per $1 for each buy that is still at least half held (a buy sold straight back earns nothing), up to {creatorFeeCapPerTraderDay} from one trader a day. Of the tokens you launch on one day, only your best {bestTokensPerDay} count. A token scores nothing if you sold or moved tokens out during the season (to any wallet, including one of your own; burning them is fine) and less than half of your own buys of it is left.

traders.question: How do traders earn?
traders.early: Be one of the first {earlyFirstBuyers} real buyers of a token that now has {earlyHoldersTarget} real holders, with your first buy this season: {early} points, and {earlyStillHolding} more while you still hold half of that first buy.
traders.hold: Every token you first buy this season, with a real first buy, and still half-hold a day later (that buy itself, not a later one; a token you already held before the season does not count): {hold} points, up to {holdTokensPerDay} tokens a day. Fees you pay buying other people's tokens with {scoutFeeMinHolders}+ real holders ({scoutFeeMinEligibleHolders}+ of them qualifying), for each buy still at least half held: {scoutFeePointsPerUsd} points per $1, up to {scoutFeeCapPerDay} a day. Trades under ${minTradeUsd} earn nothing.

board.question: Who appears on the leaderboard?
board.answer: Profiles verified with one post on X from an account at least {eligibleMinAgeDays} days old with {eligibleMinFollowers} or more followers. Everyone else can see the points waiting for them on their dashboard; while the season runs, they unlock for the whole season so far with the next points update after the profile qualifies (points update about every hour). The post itself earns nothing.

know.intro: Tokens launched here are created by their launchers, not by openlaunch. Do your own research; a locked pool does not make a token valuable. Nothing is refundable.

price.question: How does the price move?
price.curve: Price follows a single-sided Uniswap v4 curve: the first buyers get the most tokens per unit of the quote asset, and every buy moves the price up. Sells move it down.
price.snipers: There is no anti-snipe mechanism. Bots can buy in the first block like anyone else.
price.firstBuy: The launch form suggests a small first buy (about $25) so your token opens with a holder and a price; clear it and the launch stays free.

quiet.question: Why is my token under “quiet launches”?
quiet.ranking: The home page ranks by facts, not by launch order. A token is live once a wallet other than its launcher has traded it in the last 24 hours; trades in the launch block and the next three blocks (snipe bots) don't count, and neither do the launcher's own. Live tokens rank by outside wallets in the last hour, then today, then by their last outside trade. A wallet's newest launch gets its first hour on the board regardless; after that it sits under quiet launches, one row per wallet, until someone trades it.
quiet.hidden: Nothing is hidden: every launch stays in the New tab, in search and in the API. The only way up is a trade from an outside wallet.

change.question: What can change after launch?
change.answer: Nothing on-chain can be edited after launch: not the name, not the fee, not the beneficiaries. Metadata (image, description, links) is stored by this site and can change; the token itself cannot.

twig.question: What is a TWIG- or GITLAWB-quoted pool?
twig.twig: TWIG is Twigpine's token on Base: a 1:1 wrapper of GITLAWB. Anyone can wrap GITLAWB into TWIG, or unwrap it back, at any time with no fee, and every TWIG is backed by one GITLAWB held in its contract, which has no owner and no transfer restrictions. It is the quote the Base form offers: pick it and buyers pay in TWIG; any trading fee is paid in TWIG to the beneficiaries named at launch (by their shares) when it is collected, and a launch that names none has its TWIG fees burned when they are collected.
twig.gitlawb: GITLAWB is Twigpine's token on Base, bridged 1:1 to Robinhood Chain over LayerZero (one supply, two chains): an ordinary ERC-20 with no transfer restrictions and no issuer switch. The Robinhood Chain form offers it; on Base, pools already paired with GITLAWB keep their badge and price. Fees work the same way: paid in GITLAWB when collected, and a launch that names no beneficiary has its GITLAWB fees burned when they are collected.
twig.prices: Dollar figures for both come from the Uniswap v4 WETH/GITLAWB pool price on Base, cross-checked against a 30-minute on-chain average, and ETH/USD; one TWIG counts as one GITLAWB, since it unwraps to one. They are for display and sorting only; nothing on-chain depends on them.

stocks.question: What should I know about stock-quoted pools?
stocks.quotes: Stock-quoted pools use tokenized stocks as the quote asset: Coinbase tokenized stocks (B20) on Base, recognised here only from Coinbase's official list and priced in dollars where Chainlink publishes an on-chain feed (the others show no dollar price); Robinhood Stock Tokens on Robinhood Chain, recognised only from Robinhood's own registry.
stocks.securities: Both are securities issued by third parties under Regulation S and are not offered to US persons. Coinbase's also exclude the UK, Canada, Australia, Singapore and Switzerland. Their issuers can pause transfers or freeze wallets in restricted jurisdictions. Holding or trading them is subject to the issuer's terms, not ours.

contracts.heading: Don't take our word for it.
contracts.intro: Contracts, addresses and source verification. The same contract design on every chain, with chain-specific Uniswap deployments.
contracts.note: Uniswap v4's PoolManager, PositionManager, Permit2 and Universal Router are Uniswap's canonical deployments. MIT-licensed source on <github>GitHub ↗</github>; the verification records for each chain are linked above.

meta.title: About {brand}
meta.description: {brand} is a free, open-source token launchpad on Base, Robinhood Chain and Arc. What it does, who builds it, and which channels are official.

about.title: What {brand} is
about.description: {brand} is a free, open-source token launchpad. One transaction deploys a fixed-supply ERC-20, opens a Uniswap v4 pool at the market cap you pick and locks 100% of the supply as liquidity, forever. It runs on Base, Robinhood Chain and Arc.

noFee.title: No platform fee
noFee.body: The factory and the locker have no fee address, fee variable or treasury. There is nothing to switch on later.

locked.title: Liquidity locked forever
locked.body: 100% of the supply goes into one Uniswap v4 position at launch. Its NFT is held by an ownerless locker with no withdraw path: not the creator, not openlaunch, nobody.

noAdmin.title: No pre-mine, no admin
noAdmin.body: Every token starts inside the pool. The contracts have no owner, no pause, no upgrade and no allowlist. They are the same for everyone.

openSource.title: Open source
openSource.body: Contracts and site are MIT-licensed on GitHub, and every deployed contract is source-verified on the chain's explorers.

creatorFee.title: Creator-set trading fee
creatorFee.body: 0%, 1% or 3%, chosen at launch, paid in full to the beneficiaries the creator names or burned. Fixed forever.

agents.title: Open to agents
agents.body: A launch is one contract call from any wallet. The list, trades and metadata are also plain JSON, with no API key.

chains.heading: Where it runs
chains.body: The same contract design is deployed on every chain, each paired with that chain's canonical Uniswap v4 contracts. Addresses and verification records are listed on the <link>contracts section</link> of the how-it-works page.

who.heading: Who builds it
who.body: {brand} is built by Twigpine and developed in the open. The contracts, the indexer and this site live in one MIT-licensed repository; contributions go through pull requests there.
who.launchers: Tokens launched here are created by their launchers, not by {brand}. A locked pool does not make a token valuable; read <link>before you begin</link>.

official.heading: Official channels
official.body: These are the only places {brand} speaks from. Accounts, domains and repositories with similar names are not affiliated with {brand}, and {brand} is not related to other products that share the name.
official.formerly: Formerly {legacy}; the old domain redirects here.
official.original: MIT. Forks on GitHub are copies; this is the original.

meta.title: Agents
meta.description: Launch and trade tokens from an agent: one contract call, plus a JSON API for the list, trades and metadata.

agents.title: Agents
agents.description: No API key, no signup, no platform fee. A launch is one contract call from any wallet with a little ETH for gas. Everything the site shows is also JSON.
agents.entryBottom: The same protocol is yours to build with.
agents.readHint: Use the JSON API to read.
agents.writeHint: Use your wallet to write on-chain.

launch.subtitle: One call, from your own wallet.
launch.call: Call launch(params) on that chain's factory. The example below launches on Base with an ETH quote.
launch.exampleNote: Example only. Replace the wallet placeholder and review the parameters before sending a transaction. Never share your private key.
launch.quote: ETH uses address zero. For TWIG on Base (the quote the form offers there) use {twig}. For GITLAWB use {gitlawbBase} on Base (still recognised, badged and priced) or {gitlawbRobinhood} on Robinhood Chain; for USDG on Robinhood Chain, {usdg}. For any ERC-20 quote call findSalt(...) first so the token address sorts above the quote.
launch.startTick: Sets the opening market cap. A multiple of 200; 184200 ≈ 10 ETH FDV for 1B supply.
launch.recipients: Empty means fees are burned. Otherwise, shares are in bps and sum to 10000.
launch.metadata: For an image, description or links, send metadata first. The response contains the uri to pass as metadataURI and the predicted token address.
launch.firstBuy: Buy a little right after the launch confirms (a Universal Router swap on the new pool; the site's form suggests about $25). A token with no holder and no price move reads as dead on screeners and sits under quiet launches on the home page until an outside wallet trades it.

read.subtitle: JSON endpoints, plus a plain-text agent reference.
read.amounts: Raw token and quote amounts are decimal integer strings. Use quote_decimals for quote amounts, not a blanket 18 decimals. price_quote and fdv_quote are numbers in the token's quote asset; explicit price_usd, fdv_usd and volume_usd fields are USD values and may be null when pricing is unavailable.
read.polling: Poll modestly and back off on errors. Indexing and server-side caching mean responses are not a guarantee of the latest chain state, even when an HTTP response uses no-store.

trade.subtitle: Standard pools. Direct contract calls.
trade.swap: Pools are plain Uniswap v4, with tick spacing 200 and no hook. The quote can be ETH, TWIG (Base), GITLAWB (Base and Robinhood Chain), USDG (Robinhood Chain), USDC (Arc) or a supported issuer-registry stock token. Get the actual pool key with poolKeyOf(token) on the factory. Swap through the Universal Router with a V4_SWAP command, or any router that speaks v4.
trade.collect: Anyone may call collect(tokenId) on that chain's locker to pay out accrued fees. Base locker: {locker}. Use the matching chain address above.
trade.stocks: Tokenized stocks are third-party securities offered under Regulation S, not to US persons. The site recognizes them from issuer registries, not on-chain names.
trade.sync: After a transaction you sent, request immediate indexing with this endpoint. Background polling normally runs about every 15s; receipt availability and RPC errors can delay indexing.
